title: Why the forecast moved on May 17
dek: The model began using a weighted VoteHub generic-ballot average, OpenFEC finance, MIT/MEDSL Senate history, and Census population growth.
author: Senate Probability Desk
body: The May 17 run changed more than a normal daily update because the data pipeline changed. The forecast now ingests public feeds before running the Senate simulations.

The biggest new input is the weighted generic-ballot average from VoteHub. It uses recency, sample size, likely-voter status, internal and partisan penalties, and repeated-pollster downweighting instead of a plain average.

The run also uses OpenFEC candidate finance, MIT/MEDSL Senate history, and Census population-growth data. That makes the forecast more automatic, but it also means the first day after the rework should be read as a model break rather than ordinary movement.
